// lib/segment/src/types.rs line 3834-3865
#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, Validate)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields, rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub struct Filter {
    #[serde(default, with = "MaybeOneOrMany")]
    #[schemars(with = "MaybeOneOrMany<Condition>")]
    pub should: Option<Vec<Condition>>,  // <-- has MaybeOneOrMany wrapper
    pub min_should: Option<MinShould>,
    #[serde(default, with = "MaybeOneOrMany")]
    #[schemars(with = "MaybeOneOrMany<Condition>")]
    pub must: Option<Vec<Condition>>,     // <-- has MaybeOneOrMany wrapper
    pub must_not: Option<Vec<Condition>>, // <-- MISSING MaybeOneOrMany wrapper!
}

// lib/segment/src/common/utils.rs line 107-108
.seq(|x| x.deserialize().map(Some))
.map(|x| x.deserialize().map(|x| vec![x]).map(Some))  // <-- BUG: accepts single object and wraps it
source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST QueryRequestInternal.filter (lib/api/src/rest/schema.rs:582) → Filter type (lib/segment/src/types.rs:3834) → must_not: Option<Vec<Condition>> WITHOUT MaybeOneOrMany → serde still accepts single object through default deserialization fallback → BUG: Type system expects array but accepts object
source_grounding.note: Source code clearly defines must_not as Vec<Condition> without MaybeOneOrMany wrapper, while should/must have it. Despite this, REST API accepts single object through serde's fallback behavior - this is a validation gap where the API contract (Vec/array) is not enforced at runtime.
